title: On Cyber-social Learning: How to Value the Human in Computational Systems
extended_summary:
This paper argues for a “cyber-social learning” perspective that brings together cybernetic principles and the social nature of learning. The central question is how educational technology can preserve and value human agency while also taking advantage of computational systems, feedback loops, and learning analytics.

The paper is primarily conceptual rather than empirical. It draws on historical discussion of cybernetics and on examples from the Cyber-Social Learning Laboratory to illustrate how decentralized, heterarchical systems can inform educational design. It also presents a learning analytics system as an example of recursive feedback mechanisms that support and augment human feedback in formal education.

The paper positions this approach as a way to rethink education in the digital age. It claims that cyber-social environments can encourage self-regulation and collaboration while supporting individual learning pathways within community contexts. Overall, the paper concludes that cybernetic principles offer a promising avenue for designing more adaptive and effective learning experiences, and it calls for a reimagination of traditional education models.
quality_tier_rationale: This is a conference proceedings/front matter and mostly descriptive conference information plus abstracts. No clear empirical study design, comparison, or measurable intervention effects are presented in the provided text.
impact_tier_rationale: The paper does not report outcome data or any measurable impact on learners, teachers, or institutions in the text provided. It is not evidence of an intervention effect in K-12 planning/coaching cycles for generative AI feedback.
